title: Consumption & Marketing
subtitle: Debate advertising, influence, and the limits of growth

lessons.title: La publicité
lessons.description: Explore how advertising persuades — and where persuasion becomes manipulation.

blocks.heading: Les ressorts de la persuasion
blocks.body: French advertising rarely just describes a product — it builds a story around it. Copywriters lean on three classic levers: reason (chiffres, comparaisons), emotion (bonheur, peur de manquer), and repetition (un slogan martelé finit par sembler vrai). Recognising which lever is being pulled is the first step to reading an ad critically.

examples.french: Cette publicité joue sur la peur de manquer quelque chose.
examples.english: This ad plays on the fear of missing out.

examples.french: Le slogan est répété à chaque publicité, jusqu'à devenir familier.
examples.english: The slogan is repeated in every ad, until it becomes familiar.

examples.french: Les chiffres donnent une impression de sérieux.
examples.english: The figures give an impression of seriousness.

examples.french: On nous vend un mode de vie, pas seulement un produit.
examples.english: We're being sold a lifestyle, not just a product.

examples.french: Une bonne accroche capte l'attention en trois secondes.
examples.english: A good hook grabs attention in three seconds.

blocks.tip: In French, "une pub" is the everyday spoken form of "une publicité" — both are feminine.

blocks.heading: Le vocabulaire d'une campagne
blocks.body: A French ad campaign (une campagne publicitaire) usually involves an advertiser (un annonceur) who defines a target audience (un public cible), then briefs an agency to design a slogan, a logo, and a series of spots or posters. Talking about marketing in French means mastering this chain of roles.

examples.french: L'annonceur a choisi de cibler les jeunes actifs.
examples.english: The advertiser chose to target young professionals.

examples.french: Le public cible de cette marque a moins de trente ans.
examples.english: This brand's target audience is under thirty.

examples.french: L'agence a proposé un nouveau logo plus sobre.
examples.english: The agency proposed a new, more understated logo.

examples.french: Le spot publicitaire dure trente secondes.
examples.english: The ad spot lasts thirty seconds.

examples.french: L'affiche a été placardée dans tout le métro.
examples.english: The poster was plastered all over the metro.

blocks.heading: Publicité et manipulation : où est la limite ?
blocks.body: French law bans misleading advertising (la publicité trompeuse) and heavily restricts messages aimed at children, but the line between persuasion and manipulation stays blurry. Some critics argue that advertising manufactures needs by appealing to the unconscious; defenders reply that consumers remain free to choose. Both positions are worth being able to summarise in French, even if you don't share them.

examples.french: Certains estiment que la publicité crée des besoins artificiels.
examples.english: Some believe advertising creates artificial needs.

examples.french: D'autres répondent que le consommateur reste libre de choisir.
examples.english: Others reply that the consumer remains free to choose.

examples.french: Un message subliminal agit sans que l'on s'en rende compte.
examples.english: A subliminal message works without your realising it.

examples.french: La loi interdit la publicité trompeuse en France.
examples.english: The law bans misleading advertising in France.

examples.french: Le matraquage publicitaire finit par lasser le public.
examples.english: Advertising overload eventually wears the public out.

blocks.tip: "Bien que" + subjunctive is useful here: "Bien que la loi encadre la publicité, certains messages restent ambigus."

blocks.heading: Le superlatif dans les slogans
blocks.body: Advertising loves the superlative: "le plus", "la meilleure", "le seul". These forms let a brand claim the top spot without naming a competitor directly. Remember that most adjectives take "le/la/les plus + adjective", while a few (bon, mauvais) have irregular superlative forms.

examples.french: La formule la plus économique du marché.
examples.english: The most economical package on the market.

examples.french: C'est le meilleur choix pour votre famille.
examples.english: It's the best choice for your family.

examples.french: Le tissu le moins polluant jamais créé.
examples.english: The least polluting fabric ever created.

examples.french: La marque la plus recommandée par les clients.
examples.english: The brand most recommended by customers.

examples.french: Notre pire ennemi, c'est l'ennui.
examples.english: Our worst enemy is boredom.

blocks.tip: In advertising, a superlative without a clear comparison group ("le plus efficace" — than what?) is often a red flag for exaggeration.

blocks.heading: Le gérondif : en + participe présent
blocks.body: Ad copy often uses the gerund (en + present participle) to link an action to its supposed benefit: "en choisissant X, vous obtenez Y". It expresses simultaneity or means — the two things happen together, or one is achieved through the other.

examples.french: En choisissant cette marque, vous soutenez l'emploi local.
examples.english: By choosing this brand, you support local jobs.

examples.french: En regardant cette publicité, on se sent déjà séduit.
examples.english: While watching this ad, you already feel won over.

examples.french: Elle a économisé en comparant les prix.
examples.english: She saved money by comparing prices.

examples.french: En achetant maintenant, vous profitez de la promotion.
examples.english: By buying now, you benefit from the promotion.

examples.french: On convainc souvent en répétant, pas en démontrant.
examples.english: You often convince by repeating, not by proving.

passages.title: La campagne qui a fait parler
passages.french:
L'entreprise Lumiora vient de lancer une campagne publicitaire pour son eau de source « pure et essentielle ».
Sur l'affiche, une jeune femme court sur une plage déserte, une bouteille à la main, sous le slogan : « Respirez. Buvez. Vivez. »
Le spot publicitaire, diffusé pendant les journaux télévisés, a immédiatement suscité des réactions.
Des associations de consommateurs accusent Lumiora de vendre une émotion plutôt qu'un produit.
« Cette eau n'a rien de particulier, affirme Camille Vasseur, porte-parole d'une association de défense des consommateurs. Le message vise clairement l'inconscient du public. »
La directrice marketing de Lumiora, Inès Rocher, rejette cette critique.
Selon elle, la campagne ne fait que raconter une histoire, comme le font toutes les marques depuis toujours.
« Nous ne trompons personne : nous vendons de l'eau, et nous le disons clairement sur l'étiquette », précise-t-elle.
Les experts, eux, restent partagés sur la question.
Certains estiment que le matraquage publicitaire autour d'un produit aussi banal frôle la manipulation.
D'autres rappellent que le consommateur français est plutôt bien informé, et de plus en plus critique envers ce genre de message.
Même le choix du prénom « Lumiora » n'est pas un hasard : il évoque à la fois la lumière et l'or.
En attendant que le débat se calme, la notoriété de la marque a doublé en un seul mois.
Contestée ou non, la campagne semble donc avoir atteint son objectif.
passages.english:
The company Lumiora has just launched an advertising campaign for its 'pure and essential' spring water.
On the poster, a young woman runs on a deserted beach, bottle in hand, under the slogan: 'Breathe. Drink. Live.'
The ad spot, aired during the evening news, immediately sparked reactions.
Consumer associations accuse Lumiora of selling an emotion rather than a product.
'This water has nothing special about it,' states Camille Vasseur, spokesperson for a consumer advocacy group. 'The message clearly targets the public's unconscious.'
Lumiora's marketing director, Inès Rocher, rejects this criticism.
According to her, the campaign is simply telling a story, as brands have always done.
'We're deceiving no one: we sell water, and we say so clearly on the label,' she states.
Experts, for their part, remain divided on the question.
Some believe that the advertising overload around such a mundane product borders on manipulation.
Others point out that French consumers are fairly well informed, and increasingly critical of this kind of message.
Even the choice of the name 'Lumiora' is no accident: it evokes both light and gold.
While the debate simmers down, the brand's awareness has doubled in a single month.
Contested or not, the campaign therefore seems to have reached its goal.

lessons.title: Le marketing d'influence
lessons.description: Discuss influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and the debate over online authenticity.

blocks.heading: Qui sont les influenceurs ?
blocks.body: An influenceur (or influenceuse) builds an audience on a platform — Instagram, TikTok, YouTube — and monetises that audience through sponsored content. Brands pay for a post, a story, or a mention, hoping the influencer's followers will trust the recommendation more than a traditional ad.

examples.french: Cette influenceuse compte deux millions d'abonnés.
examples.english: This influencer has two million followers.

examples.french: Elle publie du contenu sponsorisé une fois par semaine.
examples.english: She posts sponsored content once a week.

examples.french: La plateforme mesure l'engagement grâce à un algorithme.
examples.english: The platform measures engagement using an algorithm.

examples.french: Un partenariat rémunéré peut porter sur un simple code promo.
examples.english: A paid partnership can be as simple as a promo code.

examples.french: Les marques préfèrent souvent les micro-influenceurs, plus proches de leur communauté.
examples.english: Brands often prefer micro-influencers, closer to their community.

blocks.tip: "Influenceur" is now standard French — the Académie française even proposed "influenceur" over anglicisms like "influencer".

blocks.heading: La transparence : une obligation, pas un choix
blocks.body: Since 2023, French law requires influencers to clearly disclose sponsored content — typically with a visible mention such as "#partenariat" or "#publicité". Undisclosed sponsorship is called "la publicité déguisée" (disguised advertising), and it can be reported and penalised.

examples.french: L'influenceur doit divulguer ses contenus commerciaux.
examples.english: The influencer must disclose their commercial content.

examples.french: La mention légale doit apparaître dès les premières secondes.
examples.english: The legal disclosure must appear within the first few seconds.

examples.french: Dissimuler un partenariat s'appelle de la publicité déguisée.
examples.english: Concealing a partnership is called disguised advertising.

examples.french: Une association a dénoncé plusieurs comptes pour ce manquement.
examples.english: An association reported several accounts for this failure.

examples.french: La transparence protège autant l'abonné que la marque.
examples.english: Transparency protects the follower as much as the brand.

blocks.heading: Le débat sur l'authenticité
blocks.body: Followers say they value authenticity, yet the most successful accounts are often the most professionally managed. Some argue that paid partnerships automatically damage credibility; others reply that an influencer can stay honest while being compensated — as long as the audience knows. Both sides deserve a fair hearing in French.

examples.french: Peut-on rester authentique tout en étant rémunéré ?
examples.english: Can you stay authentic while being paid?

examples.french: Certains estiment qu'un partenariat nuit forcément à la crédibilité.
examples.english: Some believe a partnership necessarily harms credibility.

examples.french: D'autres pensent que la confiance dépend surtout de la transparence.
examples.english: Others think trust depends mainly on transparency.

examples.french: L'image publique d'un influenceur se construit sur des années.
examples.english: An influencer's public image is built over years.

examples.french: Un avis honnête reste possible, même dans une collaboration payée.
examples.english: An honest opinion remains possible, even in a paid collaboration.

blocks.tip: Use "tout en étant" ("while being") to concede a point elegantly: "Tout en étant payée, elle garde un ton sincère."

blocks.heading: "Tout en" + gérondif : la concession simultanée
blocks.body: "Tout en" reinforces the gerund to express that two things happen at once, often with a hint of contrast: you do one thing while also, somewhat surprisingly, doing another. It is very useful for balanced arguments about influencers.

examples.french: Tout en étant payée, elle garde un ton sincère.
examples.english: While being paid, she keeps a sincere tone.

examples.french: Tout en promouvant la marque, il critique certains de ses choix.
examples.english: While promoting the brand, he criticises some of its choices.

examples.french: Elle gagne de l'argent tout en gardant la confiance de ses abonnés.
examples.english: She earns money while keeping her followers' trust.

examples.french: Tout en dénonçant la publicité déguisée, il en a lui-même profité.
examples.english: While denouncing disguised advertising, he himself benefited from it.

examples.french: Tout en respectant la loi, certains comptes restent ambigus.
examples.english: While respecting the law, some accounts remain ambiguous.

blocks.tip: Don't confuse this with plain "en + gérondif" (means/simultaneity) — "tout en" adds a note of contrast or concession.

blocks.heading: Le subjonctif après les expressions de doute
blocks.body: Verbs and expressions of doubt (douter que, il n'est pas certain que, je ne pense pas que) require the subjunctive, unlike expressions of certainty (je pense que, il est certain que), which take the indicative. This distinction matters when debating whether influencers can "really" be authentic.

examples.french: Je doute qu'un partenariat payé soit totalement objectif.
examples.english: I doubt a paid partnership is totally objective.

examples.french: Il n'est pas certain que la transparence suffise à rassurer le public.
examples.english: It isn't certain that transparency is enough to reassure the public.

examples.french: Je ne pense pas que tous les avis soient sincères.

passages.title: La mention qui manquait
passages.french:
Léa Fontaine, influenceuse beauté suivie par huit cent mille abonnés, publie chaque semaine des vidéos sur les cosmétiques naturels.
Le mois dernier, elle a présenté une nouvelle crème de la marque GlowNature sans mentionner qu'il s'agissait d'un partenariat rémunéré.
Plusieurs abonnés ont remarqué l'absence de la mention légale obligatoire.
« Le produit a l'air sincère, mais l'absence de transparence pose problème », a écrit un internaute sous la vidéo.
Face à la polémique, Léa Fontaine a reconnu son erreur et publié des excuses.
« Je pensais que ma sincérité suffisait, explique-t-elle. Je me trompais : la loi exige une mention claire, quelle que soit mon intention. »
GlowNature, de son côté, affirme avoir respecté son contrat et rejette toute responsabilité dans cette affaire.
L'association Vigie Consommateurs a rappelé que la publicité déguisée reste interdite, même sans intention de tromper.
D'autres abonnés défendent l'influenceuse, soulignant qu'elle a corrigé l'erreur rapidement et sans se cacher.
Cet incident relance un débat plus large : peut-on vraiment faire confiance à un avis rémunéré ?
Certains experts estiment que la transparence, plus que l'absence totale de rémunération, garantit la confiance du public.
D'autres jugent que tout contenu payé perd, par nature, une part de son objectivité.
Depuis cet épisode, Léa Fontaine indique systématiquement ses partenariats dès la première seconde de ses vidéos.
Son nombre d'abonnés, loin de baisser, a même légèrement augmenté.
passages.english:
Léa Fontaine, a beauty influencer followed by eight hundred thousand people, posts videos about natural cosmetics every week.
Last month, she featured a new cream from the brand GlowNature without mentioning it was a paid partnership.
Several followers noticed the absence of the mandatory legal disclosure.
'The product seems genuine, but the lack of transparency is a problem,' one user wrote under the video.
Facing the backlash, Léa Fontaine admitted her mistake and posted an apology.
'I thought my sincerity was enough,' she explains. 'I was wrong: the law requires a clear disclosure, whatever my intention.'
GlowNature, for its part, claims to have honoured its contract and denies any responsibility in this matter.
The association Vigie Consommateurs pointed out that disguised advertising remains illegal, even without intent to deceive.
Other followers defend the influencer, stressing that she corrected the mistake quickly and openly.
The incident revives a broader debate: can a paid review really be trusted?
Some experts believe that transparency, more than the total absence of payment, guarantees public trust.
Others judge that any paid content loses, by nature, some of its objectivity.
Since this episode, Léa Fontaine systematically discloses her partnerships from the very first second of her videos.
Her follower count, far from dropping, has even risen slightly.

lessons.title: La décroissance
lessons.description: Debate economic growth versus degrowth — present both sides with balance and attribution.

blocks.heading: Qu'est-ce que la décroissance ?
blocks.body: La décroissance is a school of thought that questions economic growth (mesured by le PIB) as the main measure of progress. Its supporters argue that infinite growth is impossible on a finite planet, and propose "sobriété" — a voluntary reduction in consumption — as an alternative. This is a genuine academic and political debate in France, not a fringe idea.

examples.french: La décroissance remet en question l'objectif même de croissance.
examples.english: Degrowth calls into question the very goal of growth.

examples.french: Le PIB mesure la production, pas le bien-être.
examples.english: GDP measures production, not well-being.

examples.french: Certains économistes prônent une sobriété choisie plutôt que subie.
examples.english: Some economists advocate chosen, not forced, restraint.

examples.french: L'empreinte écologique de nos modes de vie inquiète de plus en plus.
examples.english: The ecological footprint of our lifestyles is increasingly worrying.

examples.french: Les ressources naturelles ne sont pas infinies.
examples.english: Natural resources are not infinite.

blocks.tip: Economist Serge Latouche is often cited as a founding voice of the French "décroissance" movement.

blocks.heading: Les arguments des partisans
blocks.body: Supporters (les partisans) of degrowth argue that constant growth drives overconsumption and overproduction, exhausting natural resources faster than they can renew. They favour relocalising production, reducing working hours, and measuring progress with indicators other than GDP — such as a well-being index.

examples.french: Les partisans de la décroissance dénoncent la surconsommation.
examples.english: Degrowth supporters denounce overconsumption.

examples.french: La surproduction épuise les ressources plus vite qu'elles ne se renouvellent.
examples.english: Overproduction depletes resources faster than they renew.

examples.french: Ils défendent la relocalisation de la production.
examples.english: They advocate relocalising production.

examples.french: Un indicateur de bien-être vaudrait mieux qu'un simple indice de croissance.
examples.english: A well-being indicator would be better than a simple growth index.

examples.french: Pour eux, un mode de vie plus sobre peut être plus épanouissant.
examples.english: For them, a more restrained lifestyle can be more fulfilling.

blocks.heading: Les arguments des opposants
blocks.body: Opponents (les opposants) reply that growth remains the best tool against unemployment and poverty, and that degrowth policies risk a drop in purchasing power. They favour "green growth" (la croissance verte) — decoupling growth from pollution through innovation — over renouncing growth altogether. Presenting both views fairly, and attributing each to its side, is essential at B2 level.

examples.french: Les opposants craignent une hausse du chômage.
examples.english: Opponents fear a rise in unemployment.

examples.french: Selon eux, renoncer à la croissance nuirait au pouvoir d'achat.
examples.english: According to them, giving up growth would harm purchasing power.

examples.french: Ils défendent plutôt un modèle économique de croissance verte.
examples.english: They advocate a green-growth economic model instead.

examples.french: Un compromis reste possible entre les deux positions.
examples.english: A compromise remains possible between the two positions.

examples.french: Le débat oppose deux visions du progrès, pas seulement deux chiffres.
examples.english: The debate pits two visions of progress against each other, not just two figures.

blocks.tip: Signal attribution clearly: "selon les partisans...", "les opposants estiment que..." — never present one side as simply "the truth".

blocks.heading: La concession : bien que, quoique + subjonctif
blocks.body: Balanced debate requires concession: acknowledging a valid point before making your own. "Bien que" and "quoique" ("although") both introduce a concessive clause and always take the subjunctive, even though the idea itself may be a plain fact.

examples.french: Bien que la croissance ait des limites, elle reste un objectif politique majeur.
examples.english: Although growth has limits, it remains a major political goal.

examples.french: Quoique le PIB soit critiqué, il demeure l'indicateur le plus utilisé.
examples.english: Although GDP is criticised, it remains the most widely used indicator.

examples.french: Bien que les partisans aient raison sur le climat, la question de l'emploi reste entière.
examples.english: Although the supporters are right about the climate, the question of jobs remains unresolved.

examples.french: Quoiqu'elle prône la sobriété, elle reconnaît les difficultés du changement.
examples.english: Although she advocates restraint, she acknowledges the difficulties of change.

examples.french: Bien que le débat soit vif, les deux camps s'écoutent encore.
examples.english: Although the debate is heated, the two sides still listen to each other.

blocks.tip: "Quoique" elides before a vowel: "quoiqu'elle", "quoiqu'il" — don't confuse it with "quoi que" (whatever), two words.

blocks.heading: Le conditionnel pour présenter une position sans l'affirmer
blocks.body: When reporting a contested claim without endorsing it, French often uses the conditional (le conditionnel) instead of the indicative. This lets you attribute a view to a group without stating it as established fact — essential for balanced, attributed writing about degrowth.

passages.title: Verchamps sobre
passages.french:
Dans la petite ville de Verchamps, le conseil municipal a lancé un débat inhabituel : faut-il ralentir volontairement la croissance locale ?
Le projet, baptisé « Verchamps sobre », propose de réduire la consommation d'énergie et d'encourager les commerces de proximité.
L'économiste Hélène Brancourt, partisane du projet, y voit une occasion unique.
« Notre modèle économique repose sur une croissance qui épuise nos ressources, explique-t-elle. Il est temps d'essayer autre chose. »
Selon elle, un mode de vie plus sobre pourrait aussi être plus épanouissant, loin de la surconsommation.
Marc Delisle, économiste également, se montre plus prudent.
« Je ne nie pas les limites de la croissance, mais je doute qu'une décroissance locale suffise à changer la donne », affirme-t-il.
Il craint surtout que ce projet ne fragilise l'emploi dans une ville déjà touchée par le chômage.
Les deux économistes s'accordent pourtant sur un point : le PIB ne mesure pas tout.
« Un indicateur de bien-être serait sans doute plus utile », reconnaît Marc Delisle.
Les habitants, eux, restent partagés entre curiosité et scepticisme.
Certains saluent une expérience courageuse ; d'autres redoutent une baisse du pouvoir d'achat.
Le conseil municipal a finalement voté un compromis : un an d'expérimentation, suivi d'un bilan public.
Quoique le débat soit loin d'être clos, Verchamps est déjà devenue un cas d'étude pour d'autres communes.
passages.english:
In the small town of Verchamps, the town council launched an unusual debate: should local growth be voluntarily slowed down?
The project, named 'Sober Verchamps', proposes reducing energy consumption and encouraging local shops.
Economist Hélène Brancourt, a supporter of the project, sees a unique opportunity in it.
'Our economic model relies on growth that depletes our resources,' she explains. 'It's time to try something else.'
According to her, a more restrained lifestyle could also be more fulfilling, far from overconsumption.
Marc Delisle, also an economist, is more cautious.
'I don't deny the limits of growth, but I doubt that local degrowth is enough to change things,' he states.
He fears above all that this project might weaken employment in a town already affected by unemployment.
The two economists nonetheless agree on one point: GDP does not measure everything.
'A well-being indicator would probably be more useful,' Marc Delisle admits.
Residents, for their part, remain torn between curiosity and scepticism.
Some praise a courageous experiment; others fear a drop in purchasing power.
The town council ultimately voted for a compromise: one year of experimentation, followed by a public review.
Although the debate is far from over, Verchamps has already become a case study for other towns.
